items.q: Non healing mouth ulcer persisting beyond how long mandates urgent biopsy pathway?
items.exp: Two to three week persistence thresholds (guidelines use three weeks for oral lesions, two week referral windows) separate traumatic ulcers healing in days from carcinoma or major aphthous mimics needing histology.
r: Incorrect. Days is normal healing window.
Correct. Three weeks non healing biopsies.
Incorrect. Months delay worsens stage.
Incorrect. Year is negligent delay.
items.kp: Three weeks unhealed in mouth equals biopsy.

items.q: Which oral potentially malignant lesion carries highest transformation risk?
items.exp: Velvety red erythroplakia shows severe dysplasia or carcinoma in situ in majority at biopsy, far exceeding white leukoplakia risk; speckled red white lesions sit intermediate high.
r: Incorrect. White homogeneous lower risk.
Correct. Red patch highest danger.
Incorrect. Friction lesion resolves removing cause.
Incorrect. Geographic tongue benign migratory.
items.kp: Red in mouth is danger: biopsy first.

items.q: Depth of invasion in oral tongue cancer chiefly drives which management decision beyond T staging?
o: Elective neck dissection in node negative early cancers (occult metastasis risk)
items.exp: Deeper invasion (thresholds around 4 mm patterns in guidelines) predicts occult nodal spread over 20 percent, justifying elective selective neck dissection or sentinel biopsy in clinically node negative early tongue and floor cancers.
r: Incorrect. Dose not primary depth use.
Correct. Depth decides elective neck treatment.
Incorrect. Observation risks occult nodes in deep lesions.
Incorrect. Chemo not standard thin early.
items.kp: How deep decides whether silent neck gets treated.

items.q: p16 positive oropharyngeal cancer compared with HPV negative typically has which profile?
o: Younger, cystic nodes, better treatment response and prognosis
items.exp: HPV driven cancers in younger or non smoking patients metastasise to cystic nodes yet respond better to chemoradiation with superior survival, prompting de escalation research (not yet standard outside trials in many settings).
r: Incorrect. That is tobacco driven profile.
Correct. Younger, cystic nodes, better prognosis.
Incorrect. Nodes are hallmark early.
Incorrect. Survival advantage is defining.
items.kp: HPV throat cancer: bad nodes, good outcome.

items.q: Worst prognosis major upper aerodigestive subsite among these is typically which?
items.exp: Hypopharyngeal cancers present with nodal and distant spread, malnutrition and second primaries, yielding lowest survival; lip and early glottic (sparse lymphatics, early hoarseness) fare best.
r: Incorrect. Lip sun cancers cure highly.
Correct. Hypopharynx fares worst.
Incorrect. Glottic declares early by voice.
Incorrect. HPV tonsil prognosis favourable.

items.q: Squamous neck node with unknown primary: p16 positive points search where, EBV positive where?
o: p16 oropharynx (tonsil, tongue base); EBV nasopharynx
items.exp: Immunophenotyping directs occult search: HPV pathway to palatine and lingual tonsil sampling or tonsillectomy, EBV to nasopharyngeal biopsy, changing radiation fields and prognosis.
r: Incorrect. Reversed mapping.
Correct. p16 oropharynx, EBV nasopharynx.
Incorrect. Larynx usually declares by voice.
Incorrect. Skin primary exam separate.
items.kp: p16 tonsil, EBV nasopharynx: stains point home.

items.q: Before head neck radiotherapy, dental intervention matters chiefly to prevent what?
o: Osteoradionecrosis from post radiation extractions in hypovascular bone
items.exp: Radiation endarteritis makes mandible hypovascular; later extractions trigger non healing bone necrosis, so hopeless teeth are removed and fluoride trays instituted before treatment with healing interval.
r: Incorrect. Caries risk rises too but necrosis is catastrophe.
Correct. Prevent osteoradionecrosis by pre radiation clearance.
Incorrect. Cosmetic irrelevant.
Incorrect. Xerostomia persists despite dental care.
items.kp: Bad teeth out before beam saves jaw.

items.q: Field cancerisation explains which phenomenon in smokers with hypopharyngeal cancer?
o: Synchronous and metachronous second primaries across lung, oesophagus and head neck
items.exp: Shared carcinogen exposure condemns whole mucosa, so staging and follow up survey second primaries (lung commonest lethal), and cessation remains survival intervention after diagnosis.
r: Incorrect. Multiplicity is point.
Correct. Second primaries across aerodigestive field.
Incorrect. Not germline pattern.
Incorrect. Radiation second cancers are late different mechanism.
items.kp: Same smoke, many fields, many cancers.

items.q: Betel quid and areca nut chewing classically cause which premalignant oral condition restricting mouth opening?
o: Oral submucous fibrosis with blanching and trismus
items.exp: Areca alkaloids fibrose submucosa causing pale marble mucosa, burning spice intolerance and progressive trismus with high malignant transformation, prevalent in South and Southeast Asian chewers.
r: Incorrect. Leukoplakia is surface white patch separate.
Correct. Submucous fibrosis stiffens mouth.
Incorrect. Geographic tongue benign pattern.
Incorrect. Lichen planus reticular immune condition.
items.kp: Betel mouth that cannot open: submucous fibrosis.

items.q: Referred otalgia from tongue or hypopharynx cancer travels via which shared sensory pathways chiefly?
o: Glossopharyngeal (IX) and vagus (X) auricular branches (Jacobson, Arnold)
items.exp: Ear and throat share IX and X sensory supply, so normal ear examination with persistent otalgia in adult demands oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal inspection for occult cancer or neuralgia causes.
r: Incorrect. Optic is vision.
Correct. IX and X refer throat pain to ear.
Incorrect. Facial motor moves face, taste separate.
Incorrect. Smell nerve unrelated.
items.kp: Sore ear, clean ear: examine throat for cancer.
